stem:
Rina builds a row of squares with matchsticks. Shape $1$ uses $4$ sticks, shape $2$ uses $7$ sticks, and shape $3$ uses $10$ sticks.

Which countable feature produces the related number sequence $4$, $7$, $10$, $\ldots$?

options.text: Count sticks on shape $1$ only, then reuse that same count for every later shape.
Count every interior angle in any polygon from the chapter, as if that also made this sequence.
Count the matchsticks in each whole shape; repeating that same count gives $4$, $7$, $10$, $\ldots$.
Pick the printed numeral $10$ alone because it is the largest number shown.

teacher.key_rationale: The number sequence comes from counting the same structural feature in every shape — here, the matchsticks in each whole figure. Reusing only the first count, stretching the count to unrelated polygons, or grabbing the largest printed numeral all miss that link.
